{{Set infobox |name=Premiere (Japanese) |image=Premiere-Japanese-box.png |publisher=[[Decipher]] / [[Takara]] |era=[[:Category:Decipher sets|Decipher]] (1995–2001) |released=April 1997 |cards=324 (162 Light, 162 Dark) |code=GEMP set 1301 |country=Japan |language=Japanese |next=[[A New Hope (Japanese)]] |related=[[Premiere Limited]] · [[Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game]] }} '''Premiere (Japanese)''' (基本カード) is the Japanese-language edition of [[Premiere Limited]]. [[Takara]] published it in Japan in April 1997 as スターウォーズコレクションカードゲーム. It has 324 black-border cards, 162 Light Side and 162 Dark Side, 108 of each rarity. Decipher and Takara announced the partnership in December 1996. Steve Stanley, Decipher Senior Vice President and General Counsel, visited Tokyo for Takara's introduction of the set. Takara demonstrated it at the Tokyo Toy Show, 19–23 March 1997, at Tokyo Big Sight. The first three days were trade only. The last two days were open to the public. Takara's gameplay demonstrations had standing room only. Hirohisa Satoh, Jr., President of Takara Ltd., hosted the display. Takara pre-sold more than 80 percent of the print run before street date. Takara was translating the Tournament Kit. Japan was placed in the newly created Ord Mantell region on Decipher's tournament locator. A Japanese champion was expected to compete at the [[1997 Decipher World Championship]]. Takara could not ship the Japanese cards outside Japan. The English Limited set is the 1st expansion of Star Wars CCG. This printing translates that 324-card pool. GEMP loads the Japanese faces as set 1301. English-language packs from [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] through [[Endor]] were sold in Japan with a Takara overlabel on the pack. Poor translations led Japanese players to prefer the English-language cards. Takara and Decipher ended the partnership after Japanese Premiere, [[A New Hope (Japanese)|A New Hope]], [[Hoth (Japanese)|Hoth]], and the two Japanese two-player games. [[Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game]] has a separate Japanese product. Language editions are listed on [[Translations of SWCCG]]. == Packaging == Takara sold 15-card booster packs (MSRP ¥500) in 36-pack boxes. Each pack had 10 commons, 4 uncommons and 1 rare. 60-card starters (MSRP ¥1400) came in 12-deck displays. Title: R2-D2 (Artoo-Detoo) Lore:
A small-bodied droid brimming with energy, loyal to his master and brave. A Rebel spy who is strong in adversity. Though 3PO derided him as a “cold-hearted philosopher,” his personality is rather the opposite. He is somewhat restless and sometimes acts unexpectedly.
Card text:
Adds +2 to the power, maneuver and hyperspeed of the starfighter he is aboard (+3 if Red 5). When he is at a place with an access link and the opponent draws destiny, activate 1 Force if it is 1–3. If it is 4–6, draw the top card of the Reserve Deck and add it to your hand.
=== Comparison with the English printing === The Japanese lore says that 3PO derided R2-D2 as a “cold-hearted philosopher”; the English face instead calls R2-D2 the “Incorrigible counterpart of a mindless philosopher.” The Japanese game text uses アクセス・リンク (access link) for the English Scomp link and states the two results directly, without words corresponding to the English “you may.” It expressly adds the drawn Reserve Deck card to the hand. The printed numerical statistics match the inspected English face. Neither inspected face prints a Nav Computer symbol; a later rule-derived capability must not be presented as a printed icon.[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], p. 42 (Japanese card face), pp. 101–102 (checklist). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828id_/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive]. The comparison uses the [[:File:ANH-L-r2d2.gif|original English card face]]. |see_also=* [[R2-D2 (Artoo-Detoo)|English counterpart]] * [[A New Hope (Japanese)#Card list|Japanese A New Hope card list]] * [[Translations of SWCCG#Japanese|Japanese printings]] |see_also_heading=See also |has_refs=1 |extra_sections=

Statistics

The printed values and symbols are shown above. The face prints one Droid symbol and the subtype 操縦ドロイド (astromech droid). It has no printed ability number and no printed Nav Computer, Pilot or Warrior symbol. Its lore identifies a Rebel spy.[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], p. 42 (Japanese card face), pp. 101–102 (checklist). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828id_/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive]. Base landspeed is 1 under the character movement rule; this is a rule-derived value, not a printed statistic.[[Star Wars Customizable Card Game RULEBOOK 2.0#Landspeed|Rulebook 2.0, Landspeed]]: “Characters have landspeed of 1.” The 1998 Glossary states that astromech droids provide nav computers. This is a rule-derived capability, separate from the absence of a printed Nav Computer symbol on this face.[[:File:Decipher_Glossary_1998.pdf|Decipher Glossary (1998)]], pp. 15 and 94, “astromech” and “nav computer icon”. The same Glossary gives droids no ability and gives droids without armor a defense value of zero.[[:File:Decipher_Glossary_1998.pdf|Decipher Glossary (1998)]], p. 52, “droid”. |set_icon=[[File:Icon-set-A-New-Hope.png|20px|link=A New Hope Limited]] [[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]] }}

Now don't be sad about having to deploy only on [[Dagobah (location){{!}}Dagobah]] or Cloud City. That restriction can be of some use. You can deploy him on [[Dagobah (location){{!}}Dagobah]], regardless of the location deployment restrictions, a useful thing for Jedi training. Like the typical pilot, [[Son Of Skywalker]] adds two to the power of any starship he pilots. He is immune to attrition less than four. And last, you can deploy a lightsaber to the same location as [[Son Of Skywalker]]. Combos: [[Son Of Skywalker]] + Any card that allows you to peek at the top of your Reserve Deck - a guaranteed good battle destiny. [[Son Of Skywalker]] + [[Courage Of A Skywalker]] (In hand) + [[This Is More Like It]] (In hand) + [[Smoke Screen]] (In hand) - Lots of laughs for you, your opponent looses tons of force! [[Son Of Skywalker]] + [[Chewbacca]] + [[Wookiee Strangle]] + Jedi tests + Apprentice + Lots of [[At Peace]] cards - Now [[Darth Vader{{!}}Vader]] gets choked for a change!
